title: Manus MCP: What It Is and How It Works (2026 Guide)
summary: Manus MCP supports the Model Context Protocol, letting autonomous agents call external apps and read data during tasks.
body_markdown:
## What Manus MCP costs and requires


On every run, a connected chain through Manus costs credits, and **the paid tiers start at $20 a month** , so users choosing a paid plan must budget at least $20 monthly.


The Manus help page lists prices and credits, but not which plan unlocks custom MCP.

Pro entry: 20 -> 17 Pro mid: 40 -> 34 Pro high: 200 -> 167


[Manus](https://manus.im/blog/manus-100m-arr) 's[help center](https://help.manus.im/en/articles/11711111) lists three Pro tiers:


- Billed monthly they cost $20; billed annually they drop to $17 a month, a saving of $36 a year
- Billed monthly they cost $40; billed annually they drop to $34 a month, a saving of $72 a year
- Billed monthly they cost $200; billed annually they drop to $167 a month, a saving of $396 a year


Check the connector settings in your own account before you pay, because the page gives no per-plan MCP eligibility I can quote.


### Credits used by tool-heavy tasks


On the Free tier you get 300 refresh credits a day. Pro at $20 gets 4,000, Pro at $40 gets 8,000 and Pro at $200 gets 40,000, so there's no efficiency gain from choosing a higher-priced tier.


Credits meter AI usage, and a workflow vendor's live[pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) is where its current rates are published.


According to EasyClaw, a web lookup costs 10-20 credits, a research report 200-500 and an 8-slide deck 555. One deck uses more than a full day of free credits.


On the $20 Pro plan that includes 4,000 credits a month, a run is 1 credit however many steps it has, AI steps cost more by model tier, and with your own AI keys every AI step is 1 credit, so your spending is driven by AI usage, not by workflow complexity.


I couldn't find a published credit cost per MCP tool call, so measure your own chain's burn before you commit to a tier.


### What you host and maintain for Manus MCP


You run a remote MCP server. Manus connects to it, but you keep it online, patch it and rotate its credentials. **If it goes down mid-task, the agent stalls** and the credits already spent are gone.
